extracted.intended_audience: patent office classifiers, patent examiners, and patent information professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures for assigning International Patent Classification (IPC) symbols and indexing codes to patent documents, including how to choose subclasses/groups, handle multi-aspect subjects, chemical Markush claims, libraries, and presentation of symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Articles of Manufacture classification
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject of the invention concerns an article, it is classified in the place covering the article. If no place exists for the article itself, it is classified in the appropriate function-oriented place (i.e., according to the function performed by the article) or, if this is not possible, according to the field of use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a glue-dispenser specially adapted for binding books is classified in group B42C 9/00 (applying glue peculiar to bookbinding) because there is no specific place for glue-dispensers; they are classified by function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multistep processes and industrial plants classification
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject concerns a multistep process or an industrial plant (a combination of process steps or apparatus), it is classified as a whole in a place provided for such combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no place exists for the combination, classify in the place for the product obtained by the process/plant. Additionally, individual elements (e.g., a process step or a machine of the plant) that are inventive are also separately classified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details and constructional parts classification — single-subject applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Details or parts only applicable to, or specially adapted for, one kind of subject matter are classified in the details places of that kind of subject matter, if such places exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such specific details-places do not exist, classify the details/parts in the place for the main subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details and constructional parts classification — multiple-subject applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Details or parts applicable to more than one kind of subject matter are classified in the details places of more general nature, if such places exist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If general details-places do not exist, classify such details/parts according to all kinds of subject matter to which they explicitly apply. Example: groups 11/00–23/00 cover various kinds of umbrellas while group 25/00 covers details applicable to more than one kind.

rubrics_metrics.name: General chemical formulae — classify fully identified compounds
rubrics_metrics.description: For general chemical formulae (e.g., Markush claims) classification should be given to all 'fully identified' compounds that are novel and unobvious if they are specifically claimed, products of a claimed process, or derivatives of these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A compound is 'fully identified' where (a) structure is given by exact chemical name/formula or deducible from specified reactants (not more than one from alternatives), and (b) the compound is characterised by a physical property (e.g., melting point) or its preparation is described in a worked example with practical details. Compounds identified only by empirical formula are not 'fully identified'.

rubrics_metrics.name: General chemical formulae — no fully identified compounds present
rubrics_metrics.description: If no 'fully identified' compounds are disclosed (for example, computer-generated compounds without experiments), classification should be given only to compounds with exact chemical name or developed chemical formula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification in this situation should be limited to a single or a very small number of groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: General chemical formulae — only general Markush formula disclosed
rubrics_metrics.description: When only the general Markush formula is disclosed, classify in the most specific group(s) that cover all or most potential embodiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification should be limited to a single or a very small number of groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: General chemical formulae — non-obligatory classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to obligatory classification of fully identified compounds, non-obligatory classification may be made for other compounds within the scope of the general formula or compounds derived from computer-generated models when these are of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is discretionary and used when other members are of interest for search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limiting large numbers of chemical classification symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: When classifying all 'fully identified' compounds into their most specific places would lead to a high number of classification symbols (e.g., more than twenty), the classifier may reduce the number of symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may only be done when classifying fully identified compounds would lead to assigning many subgroups under a single group at the next hierarchically higher level; in that case classify at the higher group only. Otherwise assign all specific subgroups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combinatorial libraries classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Collections ('libraries') with many compounds/biological entities should have only the 'fully identified' individual members obligatorily classified into the groups that most specifically provide for them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The library as a whole is classified in an appropriate group in subclass C40B. Non-obligatory classifications may be made for other library members of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple classification necessity
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple classification (more than one classification symbol) is needed when different categories of subject matter (e.g., processes, products, apparatus, materials) for which special places exist constitute invention information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also use multiple classification when essential technical characteristics concern both function-oriented places and application places. Multiple classification facilitates search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple classification and indexing are recommended but not obligatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple classification or classification combined with indexing is recommended to indicate additional information of interest for search, but it is not obligatory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific places may contain recommendations to assist classifiers, but these do not affect the discretionary nature of non-obligatory classification/indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-aspect classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply multi-aspect classification to subject matter characterised by several aspects (e.g., intrinsic structure and particular use/property); classifying according to only one aspect leads to incomplete search information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification symbols allotted should not be restricted to places covering only one aspect; give due regard to other non-trivial aspects which may need classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indication of multi-aspect desirable places
rubrics_metrics.description: Places in the IPC where multi-aspect classification is especially desirable are indicated by a note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on the subject matter, such a note either prescribes obligatory classification according to indicated aspects or recommends multi-aspect classification to increase search efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid systems (classification + indexing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Hybrid systems consist of a classification scheme plus an associated complementary indexing scheme to improve classification effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classifying within a hybrid system, first assign all appropriate classification symbols, then add appropriate indexing codes from associated indexing schemes to identify useful search elements not covered by classification places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing code format and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing codes have a format similar to classification symbols and, within subclasses, are placed after the classification scheme with numbering normally starting at 101/00. Some subclasses are only for indexing and are indicated in their titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing subclasses may use numbering similar to standard symbols; their layout is hierarchical where possible to facilitate presentation and truncation for searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing codes only with classification symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Indexing codes can only be applied in association with classification symbols; each place where indexing codes may be used is indicated by a note or a heading linking them to classification symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An indexing code should not be used standalone; association and indication are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of indexing codes — element specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: In an indexing scheme, the hierarchically higher group is only to be used residually (to record a feature not provided in any subdivision); when indexing multiple elements, apply for each element the hierarchically lowest indexing group that provides for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not index residual matter in main groups of very wide or general scope which are mainly informative headings. Example guidance given for welding process indexing: apply specific codes (e.g., B23K 101/26 for rails) and avoid too-general codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligatory classification (invention information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Competent authorities must indicate the complete symbols of the Classification applied to the invention information; it is an obligation to allot the classification symbols representing the invention information (per Strasbourg Agreement Article 4(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invention information is represented only by classification symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-obligatory classification and indexing (additional information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional (non-trivial but non-inventive) information may be represented by classification symbols and/or indexing codes; it is desirable to classify or index such additional information when useful for search purposes, but this remains discretionary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific recommendations may exist in parts of the Classification to assist, but they do not make non-obligatory classification mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification procedure for granted patents (after search/examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: All subject matter covered by the claims of a granted patent must be classified as invention information along with any novel and unobvious constituents or components (subcombinations) of the claimed subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification should be based on the subject matter of each claim as a whole and on each inventive embodiment within a claim. Any unclaimed subject matter in the disclosure that is novel and unobvious must also be classified. Desirable to classify/index additional information if useful for search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification procedure for searched but unexamined applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All claimed subject matter that appears to be novel and unobvious in view of the search results must be classified as invention information along with any novel and unobvious constituents or components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any unclaimed subject matter that appears novel/unobvious in view of search results must also be classified. Desirable to classify/index additional information if useful for search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification procedure for unsearched patent documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For unsearched documents, all claimed subject matter that is potentially novel and unobvious in the opinion of the classifier (expert in the art) must be classified as invention information along with potentially novel/unobvious constituents or components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any unclaimed subject matter considered potentially novel/unobvious by the expert classifier must be classified. For classifiers who are not experts, use all claims to determine subject matter to be classified. Desirable to classify/index additional information if useful for search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify multiple inventive things separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent documents should not be classified as a single entity; all different inventive things (different claims, alternative variants, different categories like product and method) should be identified and separately classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If two or more inventive things are separately covered by the same group, the classification symbol for that group is allotted only once. If one inventive thing is invention information and another is only additional information in the same group, only the invention information classification is allotted.

rubrics_metrics.name: When no invention information is present
rubrics_metrics.description: If a classifier determines that no invention information is present within a patent document, at least one classification symbol must still be assigned as an invention information symbol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this circumstance, choose the portion of the disclosure the classifier determines to be most useful for search purposes for basing the classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing classifications to minimize unnecessary symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: To minimize unnecessary classification symbols, the classification of a previously published application may be reviewed when the application is granted, searched, evaluated or abandoned in order to confirm or alter its classification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note some IP offices classify an application only once and do not reconsider classification when a patent is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a subclass — hierarchical approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the invention and additional information, then use the hierarchical structure of the IPC: identify the relevant section, subsection, class, and under the selected class the subclass which most satisfactorily covers the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember that titles of sections/subsections/classes give only broad indication of scope; check subclass scope and notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a subclass — alternative methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative, often more efficient methods to determine the relevant subclass include using an alphabetical Catchword Index, text searching in the IPC or Catchword Index, and reviewing classification symbols of patent documents most related to the subject (e.g., statistical analysis of documents found).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care is needed when using other documents' classifications because those classifications may be based on different parts of their disclosures. Always verify relevance by checking hierarchical scope and classification rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checking subclass scope
rubrics_metrics.description: After identifying a subclass, check whether its scope is wide enough to cover the technical subject by consulting references and notes appearing after the subclass title and definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on titles; use notes and scope definitions to verify appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting a group — check applicable general and special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After selecting subclass, determine the relevant main group and subgroup by checking which general classification rule (common, first-place priority, last-place priority) applies in the selected subclass and whether any special rules are present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some subclasses use different general rules in different parts; if so, apply the appropriate rule at the relevant level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common rule (default) — general principles
rubrics_metrics.description: The common rule is the default and applies where no priority or special rules are specified; classification should be made in all appropriate places, based on the principle that technical subjects should be classifiable in one place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To limit unnecessary multiple classification, apply priority principles: (a) groups for more complex matter take priority over less complex (combinations over subcombinations; wholes over details), and (b) groups for more specialised subject matter take priority over less specialised. Apply multiple classification principles where subject has several aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common rule — procedural steps for detailed place selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: (a) review groups to see if only one provides for the subject — if so, use it; (b) if multiple groups provide, use principles in paragraph 142 (complexity/specialisation) to determine priority; if priority determined, select priority group (others may also be selected if useful); if no priority, apply step (c) separately for each group; (c) repeat at each hierarchical level until no further subgroups provide for the subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no specific place for a combination exists, classify according to subcombinations following priority principles; subcombinations not selected may be considered additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority classification rules — purpose and marking
rubrics_metrics.description: In certain IPC areas, priority rules (first-place or last-place) are applied to improve consistency; such areas are clearly marked by a note before the covered places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where priority rules apply, multiple classification is possible for different aspects or additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: First place priority rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the first place priority rule applies, at each hierarchical level classification is made in the first appropriate place (the first main group, then the first one-dot subgroup, etc.) until the deepest appropriate subgroup is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification schemes using this rule have a standardised sequence typically ordered from more complex/specialised at top to less complex/specialised lower. For combinations lacking a specific place, classify in the first group providing for at least one subcombination; other novel subcombinations must also be separately classified following the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Last place priority rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the last place priority rule applies, at each hierarchical level classification is made in the last appropriate place (the last main group, then the last one-dot subgroup, etc.) until the deepest appropriate subgroup is reached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In schemes with this rule, sequence often proceeds from less complex/general at top to more complex/specialised lower. For combinations lacking a specific place, classify in the last group providing for at least one subcombination; other novel subcombinations must also be separately classified following the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special classification rules override general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: In specific places, special classification rules may be used and these override the general rules; they are clearly specified in notes at the places concerned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Note 2(b) of subclass C08L specifies compositions of macromolecular compounds are classified according to the macromolecular constituent present in the highest proportion; if constituents are equal, classify according to each constituent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation order of classification symbols and indexing codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Order of symbols/codes on patent documents: (a) classification symbols representing invention information, with the symbol that most adequately represents the invention listed first; (b) classification symbols representing additional information; (c) indexing codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols/codes presented in tabular form in one or more columns, one symbol/code per line; follow column-first ordering (first column downwards, then second, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC version indicators and symbol formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: When classifying in main groups only, the version indicator of the IPC is placed in round brackets after the abbreviation 'Int.Cl.'; when classifying in the full IPC, the version indicator of each IPC symbol is placed in round brackets after the symbol. Earlier version indicators before (2006.01) should be replaced by (2006.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When classified in full IPC, display symbols in italics; when in main groups only, display in regular font. Invention information symbols are printed/displayed in bold, additional information in regular (non-bold). Sample representations are provided.
